label: suspect

unstated.what: Explicit ASC must be rendered for DuckDB even when NULLS LAST is also present, while the NULLS LAST clause itself must still be omitted. parse_one('SELECT x FROM t ORDER BY x ASC NULLS LAST').sql('duckdb') must equal 'SELECT x FROM t ORDER BY x ASC'. The instruction and the linked orderby page only discuss default_order making bare ORDER BY differ from ASC; they never mention NULLS.
unstated.quote: parse_one("SELECT x FROM t ORDER BY x ASC NULLS LAST").sql("duckdb") == "SELECT x FROM t ORDER BY x ASC"

instruction_covers: DuckDB read/write of 'order by i asc' must keep ASC, shown as SELECT i FROM RANGE(5) AS _(i) ORDER BY i ASC
Unspecified ORDER BY must stay unspecified because default_order can be DESC
The assumption that ORDER BY x ASC equals ORDER BY x is invalid for duckdb
notes: Parser._parse_ordered consumes ASC without recording it (sqlglot/parser.py:2947), and ordered_sql emits DESC only. DESC preservation and unspecified default-dialect ORDER BY already match the generator, so those tests are R3. DuckDB.NULL_ORDERING is nulls_are_last, so NULLS LAST on ASC is already suppressed by ordered_sql; a fix that only stops discarding the ASC token keeps that omission. The linked docs are not quoted, so R4 applies to the NULLS interaction: the existing dialect test at test_duckdb.py:384-388 already shows duckdb dropping NULLS LAST on ASC, which makes the combined behavior guessable rather than not_inferable.
